text: There is a pink flamingo on the Hendersons' lawn. It is, quote, 'aggressively cheerful'.
The Pattersons' mailbox is Eggshell, not Antique Ivory. I have a color chart.
Someone ran a leaf blower at 7:59 AM. Quiet hours begin at 8:00. I recorded it.
The pool needs a $4,000 repair. Or we could 'temporarily' close it until 2031.
My 14-foot inflatable Santa is up. It is October. Santa needs time to acclimate.
Trash cans were visible from the street for 11 hours on Tuesday. ELEVEN.
The neighbor's hedge is 2 inches over the 6-foot limit. I have a laser level.
We propose a $75 'Landscape Aesthetic Enhancement Fee'. It enhances nothing.
I'd like to install solar panels. They are visible from space, but not from the street.
The annual meeting has 3 attendees. Two are here for the free donuts.
My gnome collection (212) has been called 'a lot'. Is 212 a lot?
For $6,000 we'll install cameras that mostly point at raccoons.
A portable basketball hoop has remained portable in exactly one spot for nine months.
The new front door is Ocean Mist. The approved color is Coastal Whisper.
A corgi has been seen off leash. Witnesses describe the suspect as extremely approachable.
A garage door stayed open for forty-three minutes, exposing an unapproved kayak.
The block party needs $900 for a band whose only song is Sweet Caroline.
The community garden contains tomatoes taller than the approved shrub line.
An RV has occupied a driveway for nine days. The owner is housing family displaced by a flooded apartment, but its slide-out blocks part of the sidewalk.
rule: RVs: 72 hours maximum; sidewalks must remain clear.
evidence: Dated photos confirm nine days. Emergency housing letter is valid.

text: A new retaining wall is approved and attractive, but redirects stormwater into the neighbor's yard during heavy rain.
rule: Approved work cannot alter drainage onto another lot.
evidence: Permit passed design review; engineer confirms harmful runoff.

text: A home bakery makes six morning deliveries a day. It creates jobs and excellent muffins, plus one delivery van occasionally blocks a fire lane.
rule: Home businesses allowed; commercial traffic cannot obstruct access.
evidence: Traffic log: 31 compliant deliveries, 3 fire-lane obstructions.

text: A protected oak lifts the sidewalk two inches. Removing it violates the canopy plan; leaving it creates a trip hazard.
rule: Heritage trees protected; HOA must maintain safe common paths.
evidence: Arborist says root-friendly rerouting preserves the tree but costs $3,200.

text: A resident installed an EV charger without approval. The electrical permit is valid, but its bright cable crosses a shared walkway.
rule: Chargers are protected improvements; common paths must stay unobstructed.
evidence: Licensed installation. Cable cover fails accessibility clearance.

text: The busiest dog-walking loop has no waste station. Complaints are rising, but the proposed station sits beside Linda's prized roses.
rule: Common areas must provide sanitation without creating a nuisance.
evidence: Usage survey favors the site; alternate location adds $900 in path work.

text: A homeowner rented for three weekends while caring for a parent out of state. Guests were quiet, but rentals under 30 days are prohibited.
rule: Minimum lease: 30 days. Hardship waivers require advance approval.
evidence: Door-camera dates verified; no noise or parking complaints.

text: A permitted home battery is screened from view, but the screening hedge reduces required emergency clearance by eight inches.
rule: Energy equipment allowed; fire clearance overrides landscaping rules.
evidence: Battery permit valid. Fire marshal requests hedge trimming, not removal.
